$comment: This package has NO stylesheet. It writes its CSS through
does not exist and the coverage check in selector-integrity.mjs has nothing
to walk. P3-05 recorded that as a gap: the package depended on
P3-08 makes the gap concrete rather than theoretical, because the debugger
wiring depends on two UPSTREAM classes, not CodeMirror's own. Both are
listed below. `file` names the TypeScript module instead of a stylesheet,
which the harness treats as a label and nothing more.
Both entries carry `state: debugger-stopped`, a precondition the harness
cannot create: it needs a notebook, a kernel with debugpy, a breakpoint and
a stopped thread. So both report as SKIPPED with that reason. That is the
point — a skip names the thing nobody is checking, where silence would not.
Driving it by hand is written up in TODO.md P3-08.
scope: CodeMirror EditorView.baseTheme (no theme-name scope; see D-003 note below)

selectors.note: Upstream's own breakpoint gutter column. We hide it and replace it with .cm-d4n-breakpointGutter (D-035). It is ALSO the signal debugBridge.ts uses to decide which editors the debugger drives, so a rename costs us twice: the gutter is never mounted and upstream's own renders instead. That degrades to stock JupyterLab rather than breaking, which is the AC10 answer, but it is a silent loss of the design.

Upstream's execution-line class. Its outline and text-shadow are suppressed where our own .cm-d4n-executionLine is present. A rename leaves upstream's brown --md-brown-100 outline drawn on top of our warning tint.
